2027-01-01.title: Mary, the Holy Mother of God · Solemnity · Octave Day of Christmas
readings: The Lord bless you and keep you
May God be gracious to us and bless us
God sent his Son, born of a woman
Mary treasured all these words; the child was named Jesus
2027-01-01.alt: Holy day of obligation in many countries (check your diocese). World Day of Prayer for Peace. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-01.verse: But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
theo: The Church begins the civil year not with fireworks but with a mother. On the eighth day of Christmas she proclaims the oldest Marian title of all: Mary is Theotokos, Mother of God. The Council of Ephesus (431) defended this title against those who wished to call her only the mother of the man Jesus. The Church answered: the child she bore is one Person, the eternal Son, true God and true man; so she is truly the Mother of God (CCC 495). To honour Mary is to confess who Jesus is.

St Paul gives the shortest Christmas creed in the New Testament: “when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law.” God's eternity enters time through the yes of one woman. And the purpose is our adoption: “so that we might receive adoption as children.” Because of Mary's Son, the Spirit cries in our hearts, “Abba! Father!” The first reading puts the priestly blessing of Aaron on our lips for the new year: “The LORD bless you and keep you.” In Christ that blessing has a face.

In the Gospel the shepherds find “Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in the manger.” Everyone is amazed, “But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.” On the eighth day the child is circumcised and receives the name Jesus, “the name given by the angel”. The year opens with a Name that means “the Lord saves”, and with a mother who keeps God's deeds in her heart. St Paul VI made this day the World Day of Peace; Mary, Queen of Peace, teaches us to receive the Prince of Peace.
conn: Theotokos.
Greek for “God-bearer”. The Council of Ephesus (431) proclaimed it; the people of Ephesus carried the bishops through the streets with torches in joy (CCC 466, 495).
The priestly blessing.
Numbers 6:24–26 is the oldest biblical text found outside the Bible: two small silver scrolls from about 600 BC found at Ketef Hinnom in Jerusalem carry these words.
The eighth day.
Circumcision on the eighth day (Genesis 17:12; Leviticus 12:3) brought a boy into the covenant. Jesus, born under the Law, keeps it faithfully in order to redeem those under the Law.
The Name.
Yeshua means “the LORD saves” (Matthew 1:21). Every knee bends at this name (Philippians 2:10). The Church keeps the Most Holy Name of Jesus as an optional memorial on 3 January.
World Day of Peace.
St Paul VI instituted it in 1968. Each year the Pope publishes a message for 1 January.
Pondering.
The Greek word in Luke 2:19 means “to throw together”: Mary puts events side by side and seeks their meaning in God. She is the model of meditation on the Word.
altar: At the altar we receive the same Body that Mary carried in her womb and held in her arms. Each Communion makes us, in a small way, bearers of God.
The priest ends Mass with a blessing. Today let it echo the blessing of Aaron: the Lord bless you and keep you through this whole year.
outline: Ask: how did you begin the new year? With whom?
Mary's title protects the truth about Jesus.
Born of a woman so that we may cry Abba.
The Lord bless you and keep you.
Mary pondering by the manger while the shepherds go out praising.
live: Begin the year with a blessing (Numbers 6:24–26)
Parents, bless each child tonight with the words of Aaron.
Ponder like Mary (Luke 2:19)
Keep a small notebook this year: one line each day on what God did.
Pray for peace
Pray one decade of the Rosary today for peace in the world and in your family.
Honour the Name
Bow your head each time you say or hear the name of Jesus.
fathers: If anyone does not confess that Emmanuel is truly God, and that the holy Virgin is therefore Mother of God, for she bore according to the flesh the Word of God made flesh, let him be anathema.
Mary is the type of the Church: virgin and mother, she bore Christ, as the Church brings forth children by water and the Spirit.
magis: Mary is truly Theotokos, Mother of God.
Mary, Mother of God and of the Church, model of faith and charity.
1 January restored as the solemnity of Mary's divine motherhood.
Mary, Mother of God and Mother of the Church.
saints: 2 Jan: Sts Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen. 3 Jan: Epiphany of the Lord (in India). 7 Jan: St Raymond of Penyafort.
2027-01-01.prayer: O God, who through the fruitful virginity of Blessed Mary bestowed on the human race the grace of eternal salvation, grant, we pray, that we may experience the intercession of her, through whom we were found worthy to receive the author of life, our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son. Who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

2027-01-03.title: The Epiphany of the Lord · Solemnity
readings: The glory of the Lord has risen upon you
Every nation on earth will adore you, Lord
We observed his star and have come to pay him homage
2027-01-03.alt: In India and many other countries the Epiphany is kept on the Sunday between 2 and 8 January. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-03.verse: When they saw that the star had stopped, they were overwhelmed with joy. On entering the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother; and they knelt down and paid him homage. Then, opening their treasure chests, they offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
theo: Epiphany means “manifestation”. At Christmas the Lord was revealed to the shepherds of Israel; today he is revealed to the nations, represented by the Magi from the East. Isaiah saw it centuries before: “Arise, shine; for your light has come… Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.” Camels from Midian and Sheba bring “gold and frankincense”. St Paul names the mystery hidden for ages: “the Gentiles have become fellow heirs, members of the same body, and sharers in the promise in Christ Jesus.” Today is the feast of all of us who are not descended from Abraham, and who have been brought into God's family.

The Magi follow a star; they read the book of creation honestly, and it leads them to Jerusalem. There they need the Scriptures to find the exact place: Bethlehem, as the prophet Micah wrote. Reason and revelation work together. Yet the scribes who knew the Scriptures did not take the few hours' walk to Bethlehem, and Herod, who heard the same news, felt threatened and planned murder. The same Christ draws some to worship and provokes others to fear. Knowledge without worship leaves us where we are.

“They knelt down and paid him homage.” The journey ends in adoration. The gifts became, in the Fathers, a confession of faith: gold for a king, frankincense for God, myrrh for one who would die (St Irenaeus, St Gregory the Great). And “they left for their own country by another road.” Whoever truly meets Christ cannot go back the same way. The Church in India, born from the faith of the Apostle Thomas and the missions of Francis Xavier, is itself a fruit of the Epiphany: the light reached the East.
conn: Who were the Magi?

Probably astrologer-priests from Persia or Babylon. Tradition later counted three (from the three gifts) and called them kings (from Psalm 72:10–11 and Isaiah 60:3). The names Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar appear in the sixth century.
The star.
Numbers 24:17 had foretold: “a star shall come out of Jacob.” Whatever its natural explanation, Matthew presents it as God speaking to the nations in their own language.
Bethlehem.
Micah 5:2 names Bethlehem of Judah, David's town, as the birthplace of the ruler of Israel. The chief priests and scribes quote it to Herod.
Three manifestations.

The ancient Church celebrates three epiphanies together: the Magi, the Baptism in the Jordan and the wedding at Cana (antiphon of the Magnificat). The Eastern Churches put the Baptism at the centre (Denha).
Announcing Easter.
On the Epiphany the deacon or cantor may proclaim the date of Easter and the movable feasts. In 2027 Easter falls on 28 March, and Ash Wednesday on 10 February.
Chalk blessing.
In many places doors are marked with 20 + C + M + B + 27: the initials of the Magi, and also of Christus mansionem benedicat, may Christ bless this house.
altar: The Magi brought gold, frankincense and myrrh. At the offertory we bring bread and wine, and with them our lives. God gives back his Son.
Like the Magi we kneel before the same Child, now hidden under the sign of bread, and we too return home by another road.
outline: Ask: have you ever followed a sign that led you somewhere unexpected?
The nations come to the light; we are the Gentiles who have been invited.
Point 2 · Seeking with star and Scripture
Reason and revelation lead the Magi; the scribes stay home.
The journey ends in worship and begins a new life.
Three travellers kneeling in a poor house before a child and his mother.
“They left for their own country by another road.”
live: Bless your home
Mark your door with chalk: 20 + C + M + B + 27, and pray for all who enter.
Bring a gift (Matthew 2:11)
Offer Christ one concrete gift this week: time, money for the poor, a habit given up.
Seek him honestly
Read one chapter of a Gospel each day this month, like the Magi searching.
Pray for the missions
Pray for those who do not yet know Christ, and support the Holy Childhood or a mission collection.
fathers: Let all peoples come and adore their Creator: the Magi stand for the whole multitude of the nations who are to believe.
The Magi offered gold to the king, incense to God and myrrh to the one who was to die.
magis: The Epiphany: the great multitude of the nations enters the family of the patriarchs.
Christ the light of the nations; all are called to the people of God.
The pilgrim Church is missionary by her very nature.
The Magi as men of restless hearts seeking God.
saints: 4 Jan: Christmas weekday. 7 Jan: St Raymond of Penyafort. 10 Jan: Baptism of the Lord.
2027-01-03.prayer: O God, who on this day revealed your Only Begotten Son to the nations by the guidance of a star, grant in your mercy that we, who know you already by faith, may be brought to behold the beauty of your sublime glory. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

2027-01-06.title: 6 January · Wednesday after the Epiphany
readings: Every nation on earth will adore you, Lord
Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid
2027-01-06.alt: Christmas weekday. In countries where the Epiphany is not transferred to Sunday, today is the Solemnity of the Epiphany; the Eastern Churches celebrate the Baptism of the Lord (Denha). Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-06.verse: There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear; for fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not reached perfection in love.
theo: After feeding the five thousand, Jesus sends the disciples ahead by boat and goes up the mountain to pray. In the night the wind is against them and they strain at the oars. Early in the morning he comes to them walking on the sea. They think he is a ghost and cry out in terror. Then comes one of the most beautiful sentences in the Gospels: “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.” In Greek, “it is I” is egō eimi, the name God revealed to Moses. He climbs into the boat, and the wind ceases.

Mark adds an honest note: “they did not understand about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.” They had just seen a miracle and still did not see who Jesus was. St John gives the remedy for fear: “There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear.” God's love living in us, and our love for one another, is the only lasting answer to the storms of life. “No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God lives in us.”
outline: Ask: what are you most afraid of this year?
Jesus on the mountain sees them straining.
God's love in us is the answer.
“Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
live: Name your fear
Tell Jesus in prayer the one fear that troubles you most this year.
Love casts out fear (1 John 4:18)
Do one act of love today toward someone you are afraid of or avoid.
2027-01-06.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw your disciples straining at the oars and came to them across the sea. When the wind is against me, let me hear your voice: Take heart, it is I. Fill me with your perfect love that casts out fear. Amen.
altar: At Mass, after the Our Father, the priest prays that we may be “safe from all distress”. Christ steps into the boat of our lives in Holy Communion.

2027-01-02.title: 2 January · Saints Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen, Bishops and Doctors · Memorial
readings: Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you
All the ends of the earth have seen the victory of our God
I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness
2027-01-02.verse: John answered them, “I baptize with water. Among you stands one whom you do not know, the one who is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thong of his sandal.”
theo: The priests and Levites ask John the Baptist, “Who are you?” He answers first with what he is not: not the Messiah, not Elijah, not the prophet. Then he says who he is: “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness.” A voice exists for a word. John's whole identity is to point to another: “Among you stands one whom you do not know.” Humility is not thinking little of ourselves; it is knowing that our life is for Christ.

St John warns that whoever denies the Son does not have the Father, and urges: “Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you.” Today we honour two friends who defended that faith from the beginning: St Basil the Great and St Gregory Nazianzen, students together in Athens, monks together, then bishops in Cappadocia. Against the Arians they defended the full divinity of the Son and of the Holy Spirit; the Creed we say on Sundays owes much to them. Gregory wrote of their friendship: we knew only two roads, the one to the church and the one to the schools.
outline: Ask: if someone asked “Who are you?”, what would you answer?
Point 1 · A voice for the Word
Point 2 · Abide in what you heard
Faithful to the faith of the Apostles.
Basil and Gregory: friends who led each other to God.
“Among you stands one whom you do not know.”
live: Make way for Christ (John 1:23)
In one conversation today, point to Christ rather than to yourself.
Thank God for a friend
Pray for a friend who has helped your faith.
2027-01-02.prayer: O God, who were pleased to give light to your Church by the example and teaching of the Bishops Saints Basil and Gregory, grant that in humility we may learn your truth and practise it faithfully in charity. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
altar: At the altar the priest, like John, says “Behold the Lamb of God”: he points away from himself to Christ.

2027-01-04.title: 4 January · Monday after the Epiphany
readings: Test the spirits to see whether they are from God
I will give you the nations for your inheritance
The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light
2027-01-04.alt: Christmas weekday after the Epiphany. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-04.verse: From that time Jesus began to proclaim, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
theo: After the Epiphany the Gospel shows the light moving out into the world. Jesus leaves Nazareth and settles in Capernaum, in “Galilee of the Gentiles”, a border land mixed with pagans. Matthew sees Isaiah fulfilled: “the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light.” The first word of his preaching is “Repent”, turn around, because the kingdom has come near. Then he goes through Galilee teaching, proclaiming and curing “every disease and every sickness”, and crowds come even from the Decapolis and beyond the Jordan.

St John gives a rule for discernment: “do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits.” The test is Christ: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God. Many voices offer light today; not all lead to the Light. And John adds a word of courage to the small community: “the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.”
outline: Ask: what does a dark room feel like when someone switches on the light?
Jesus begins in a mixed, despised region.
The first word of the kingdom.
Christ in the flesh is the measure.
“Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
live: Turn around (Matthew 4:17)
Name one habit that turns you away from God and take one step back today.
Test the voices (1 John 4:1)
Before sharing a religious message on WhatsApp, check it against the teaching of the Church.
2027-01-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, you began your preaching in Galilee of the Gentiles. Shine into the dark places of my life, turn my heart back to you, and teach me to recognise your Spirit. Amen.
altar: Each Mass begins with a call to repentance: “Let us acknowledge our sins.” We answer the first word of Jesus' preaching before we receive the Bread of life.

2027-01-05.title: 5 January · Tuesday after the Epiphany
readings: Every nation on earth will adore you, Lord
He had compassion for them; the loaves are multiplied
2027-01-05.alt: Christmas weekday after the Epiphany. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-05.verse: In this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
theo: St John writes the three words that sum up the Bible: “God is love.” He does not say only that God loves, but that love is what God is: the eternal exchange of Father, Son and Spirit. And he shows where we see it: “not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son.” Love begins with God, not with us. Our love is always an answer.

Mark shows that love in action. Jesus sees a great crowd, and “he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd.” First he feeds them with his word; then, when evening comes, he feeds them with bread. The disciples want to send the people away; Jesus says, “You give them something to eat.” Five loaves and two fish, blessed, broken and given, become enough for five thousand, with twelve baskets left over. The words he uses, took, blessed, broke, gave, are the words of the Last Supper. Every Eucharist is this compassion of the Shepherd.
outline: Ask: when did someone notice your need before you asked?
live: Share bread (Mark 6:37)
Give a meal or groceries to a family in need this week.
Answer love (1 John 4:10)
Thank God for one way he loved you first.
2027-01-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you had compassion on the hungry crowd. Take my five loaves and two fish, bless them and use them for others, and teach me to love as you have loved me. Amen.
altar: At every Mass the priest takes the bread, blesses, breaks and gives. The miracle of the loaves continues: the Shepherd feeds his flock with himself.

2027-01-07.title: 7 January · Thursday after the Epiphany
readings: Whoever loves God must love his brother also
Every nation on earth will adore you, Lord
Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing
2027-01-07.alt: Optional memorial: St Raymond of Penyafort, priest. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-07.verse: Then he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
theo: Jesus returns to Galilee “filled with the power of the Spirit” and goes to the synagogue of Nazareth on the sabbath. He is handed the scroll of Isaiah and reads: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor.” Then he rolls up the scroll, sits down, and says: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.” The Anointed One, the Christ, is standing in front of them. His mission is good news for the poor, release for captives, sight for the blind, freedom for the oppressed, a year of the Lord's favour.

St John draws the consequence for us: “We love because he first loved us.” And he forbids a split between love of God and love of neighbour: “those who do not love a brother or sister whom they have seen, cannot love God whom they have not seen.” Faith that is born of God “conquers the world”. St Raymond of Penyafort, a Dominican of Barcelona, compiled the Church's laws and was a great confessor; he helped found the Mercedarians, who ransomed Christian captives. He lived the programme of Nazareth: freedom for prisoners, mercy for sinners.
outline: Ask: what would change if God's word were fulfilled “today” in your life?
Jesus is the Christ, the Anointed.
God's word is not only for the past.
Point 3 · Love the brother you see
Love of God and neighbour cannot be split.
“Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
live: Good news to the poor (Luke 4:18)
Visit, help or speak kindly to one poor person today.
Love the one you see (1 John 4:20)
Make peace with a family member you have been cold towards.
2027-01-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, anointed by the Spirit, you brought good news to the poor and freedom to captives. Let your word be fulfilled today in my life, and teach me to love the brother and sister I see, so that I may truly love God whom I do not see. Amen.
altar: In the Liturgy of the Word Christ himself speaks when the Scriptures are read (Sacrosanctum Concilium 7). Each Mass is a “today” of his word.

2027-01-08.title: 8 January · Friday after the Epiphany
readings: Whoever has the Son has life
Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean
2027-01-08.alt: Christmas weekday after the Epiphany. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-08.verse: Then Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, “I do choose. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
theo: A man “covered with leprosy” sees Jesus, falls on his face and begs: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.” He has no doubt about Jesus' power; he only asks about his will. And Jesus answers with a touch before a word. To touch a leper was forbidden and made a person unclean. But here holiness is contagious, not uncleanness: “I do choose. Be made clean.” Then Jesus sends him to the priest, so that he may be restored to the community.

Luke adds that the news spread and crowds came, “But he would withdraw to deserted places and pray.” Power and prayer go together in Jesus. St John speaks of three witnesses, “the Spirit and the water and the blood”, and of the testimony of God: “God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life.” The Fathers saw in the water and blood the sacraments of Baptism and the Eucharist, by which Christ still touches and heals us.
outline: Ask: is there something in your life you feel too ashamed to bring to Jesus?
Faith in his power, trust in his will.
Point 3 · Whoever has the Son has life
live: Bring your leprosy
Bring to confession the sin you are most ashamed of.
Touch the untouchable
Visit a patient no one visits, or greet someone others avoid.
2027-01-08.prayer: Lord Jesus, if you choose, you can make me clean. Stretch out your hand and touch what is broken in me. Let me never be ashamed to come to you, and let me bring your healing touch to others. Amen.
altar: The words before Communion echo the leper's faith: “Lord, I am not worthy… but only say the word and my soul shall be healed.”

2027-01-09.title: 9 January · Saturday after the Epiphany
readings: If we ask anything according to his will, he hears us
The Lord takes delight in his people
He must increase, but I must decrease
2027-01-09.alt: Christmas weekday after the Epiphany. Liturgical colour: white. Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary is not kept in the Christmas season.
2027-01-09.verse: He who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. For this reason my joy has been fulfilled. He must increase, but I must decrease.
theo: John the Baptist's disciples are upset: everyone is now going to Jesus. John answers with one of the most generous sentences in the Bible. He calls Jesus the Bridegroom, the title God used for himself with Israel, and calls himself only “the friend of the bridegroom”, who rejoices to hear his voice. “For this reason my joy has been fulfilled. He must increase, but I must decrease.” Jealousy in ministry and in families is overcome by joy that Christ is loved.

St John ends his letter with confidence in prayer: “if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.” He asks us to pray for a brother who sins, and he closes with a short warning: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” An idol is anything we put in God's place: money, reputation, a person, our own importance. The Baptist's way, letting Christ grow and ourselves grow smaller, is the surest protection against idols. Tomorrow we celebrate the Baptism of the Lord, where John's ministry reaches its high point.
outline: Ask: how do you feel when someone else gets the credit?
Jesus is God's spouse for his people.
The joy of the best man.
“He must increase, but I must decrease.”
live: Rejoice in others' gifts (John 3:29)
Praise sincerely someone whose success you envy.
Name your idol (1 John 5:21)
Ask: what takes God's place in my life? Give it back to him.
2027-01-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, Bridegroom of the Church, let me rejoice to hear your voice. May you increase in my life and I decrease. Keep me from idols, and teach me to ask according to your will. Amen.
altar: The Church is the bride, and the Eucharist is the wedding feast of the Lamb (Revelation 19:9). At each Mass the Bridegroom gives himself to his bride.

quick: Mary is truly the Mother of God, because her Son is God.
God sent his Son so that we may become his children.
The new year begins with the blessing of the Lord and the name of Jesus.
2027-01-01.action: Bless each member of your family with the words of Numbers 6:24–26.
2027-01-01.question: What will I ponder in my heart this year, as Mary did?
catechism: Mary is truly Mother of God.
kidsaint: She held Jesus in her arms and kept all his words in her heart. Lesson: we can talk to Jesus quietly in our heart every day.
2027-01-01.special: Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God. Octave Day of Christmas. World Day of Peace. Colour: white.
term: Greek for “God-bearer”: Mary bore the eternal Son in his human nature, so she is truly Mother of God (CCC 495).

family.explain: The shepherds found baby Jesus with Mary and Joseph. Mary kept everything in her heart and thought about it. On the eighth day the baby was named Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for peace in the world and in our home this year.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing God did for our family last year?”

illus: A grandmother in Thrissur kept a small diary for fifty years. Each night she wrote one line: what God had done that day. When she died, her grandchildren read it and found a whole family history of grace: births, illnesses healed, quarrels mended. She had pondered, like Mary, and her family discovered how faithful God had been.

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God, you kept the words of your Son in your heart. On this first day of the year we gather with you around Jesus. Lord, bless us and keep us, and give us your peace. Amen.
share: “The LORD bless you and keep you” (Numbers 6:24). Which blessing of last year am I most grateful for?
Mary pondered all these things (Luke 2:19). How can I make silence for God this year?
God sent his Son so that we might be his children (Galatians 4:4–7). What does it mean to me to call God Abba?
pm.resp: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may bring Christ to the world.
For peace among nations, and for an end to war and violence.
For our families, that the Lord may bless and keep them all through this year.
For mothers, especially those who are expecting a child or who grieve a child.
For our group, that we may ponder the Word each day.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave us your Son through the Virgin Mary. Through her prayers bless this new year, keep us in your love and give us your peace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ is revealed to all the nations.
The Magi seek with the star and find with the Scriptures.
Whoever adores Christ goes home by another road.
2027-01-03.action: Offer Christ one concrete gift this week.
2027-01-03.question: What is the star God is using to lead me to Christ, and am I following it?
kidsaint: Wise men who travelled very far following a star to find baby Jesus, and gave him their best gifts. Lesson: give Jesus your best, not your leftovers.
2027-01-03.special: Solemnity of the Epiphany of the Lord. Proclamation of the date of Easter 2027 (28 March). Colour: white.
term: Greek for “manifestation”: Christ is shown as Saviour of all nations in the Magi, at the Jordan and at Cana (CCC 528).

family.explain: Wise men from far away saw a special star. They followed it to Bethlehem, found baby Jesus with Mary, knelt down and gave him gold, frankincense and myrrh.
family.intention: We pray for people in every country who do not yet know Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift can each of us give Jesus this week?”

illus: A young engineer from Chennai, working abroad, began reading the Gospels only out of curiosity about the churches he saw. One verse led to another, a parish priest answered his questions, and two years later he was baptised at the Easter Vigil. He said: I was not looking for a religion, I was following a light, and it stopped over a Person.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, you drew the Magi from the East by a star. Draw us too, and receive the gifts of our hearts. Amen.
share: Isaiah says, “Arise, shine; for your light has come” (Isaiah 60:1). Where has Christ's light come into my life?
The Magi searched; the scribes stayed home (Matthew 2:4–6). Am I a seeker or a spectator?
They went home by another road (Matthew 2:12). What must change after I meet Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, every nation on earth will adore you.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a light to every nation.
For missionaries, especially in India and Asia.
For those who search for God sincerely, that they may find Christ.
For rulers who feel threatened by the truth, like Herod, that they may be converted.
For our group, that we may offer Christ our gold, frankincense and myrrh.
pm.close: Lord God, you led the Magi by a star to your Son. Lead us by faith to see your glory, and send us home by another road, changed by your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus prays on the mountain and sees us straining.
He comes across the storm: it is I, do not be afraid.
Perfect love casts out fear.
2027-01-06.action: Tell Jesus the one fear that troubles you most this year.
2027-01-06.question: Do I trust that Jesus sees me when I am straining at the oars?

family.explain: The disciples were in a boat in a strong wind at night. Jesus came walking on the water and said: do not be afraid, it is me! He got into the boat and the wind stopped.
family.intention: We pray for fishermen and all who travel by sea.
family.ask: Ask: “When do you feel afraid? Let us tell Jesus about it.”

illus: A fisherman from Vizhinjam was caught by a cyclone far from shore. For two nights he and his companions tied themselves to their boat. He said afterwards: I kept saying one line I learned as a child, Jesus, I trust in you. The wind did not stop at once, but the fear did.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you come to us in every storm and say: Take heart, it is I. Calm our hearts as we gather, and fill us with your love. Amen.
share: Jesus went up the mountain to pray (Mark 6:46). Do I believe that he prays for me?
Take heart, it is I (Mark 6:50). In what storm do I need to hear these words?
Perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18). How can love overcome a fear in my life?
interc: For the Church in times of persecution, that she may not be afraid.
For fishermen, sailors and all who travel.
For those who live in fear: of illness, of debt, of violence.
For families going through storms.
For our group, that our love may drive out fear.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son came to his disciples across the stormy sea. Come to us in our fears, and let your perfect love make us brave. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: John the Baptist is a voice that points to Christ.
Remain in the faith you received from the beginning.
Basil and Gregory, holy friends, defended faith in the Trinity.
2027-01-02.action: In one conversation today, point to Christ rather than to yourself.
2027-01-02.question: Does my life point to Christ or to myself?

family.explain: People asked John the Baptist if he was the Messiah. He said no: I am only a voice. Jesus is the one who is coming.
family.intention: We pray for our friends, that we may help each other to be good.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is a friend that helps me to love Jesus?”

illus: A sign at a railway crossing in Kerala reads only “Stop, look, go.” Nobody admires the sign; everyone obeys it and looks at the train. John the Baptist was content to be such a sign: people looked past him and saw Jesus.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, John the Baptist was the voice and you are the Word. Help us to point to you in all we say and do. Amen.
share: John said, “I am the voice” (John 1:23). How can my words make way for Jesus?
Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you (1 John 2:24). Who first taught me the faith?
Basil and Gregory were friends in God. Who is a friend who helps my faith?
interc: For bishops and teachers of the faith, that they may hand on the truth with love.
For theologians, that like Basil and Gregory they may serve the Church.
For friendships, that they may lead people to God.
For those who have abandoned the faith, that what they heard from the beginning may return to them.
For our group, that we may be voices for Christ.
pm.close: Lord God, you raised up Saints Basil and Gregory to defend the truth. Keep us faithful to the faith we received, and make us humble witnesses of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus begins his preaching where people sit in darkness.
His first word is: repent.
Test every spirit by Christ who came in the flesh.
2027-01-04.action: Name one habit that turns you away from God and take one step back today.
2027-01-04.question: Where in my life am I still sitting in darkness?

family.explain: Jesus went to live in Capernaum by the lake. People there were sad and in darkness, but Jesus came like a great light. He said: turn back to God!
family.intention: We pray for people who feel sad or lost.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do to bring a little light to someone this week?”

illus: During a power cut in a hostel in Kottayam, the students sat in complete darkness. One boy lit a single candle and placed it in the corridor. Within minutes everyone had gathered around it, and someone began a song. One small light changed the whole evening. Jesus came to Galilee as such a light.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the great light that dawned on those who sat in darkness. Shine on us as we gather, and turn our hearts to you. Amen.
share: The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light (Matthew 4:16). Where has Christ brought light to me?
Jesus' first word is “Repent” (Matthew 4:17). What do I need to turn away from?
Test the spirits (1 John 4:1). How do I know which voices to follow?
interc: For those who preach the Gospel, that they may call people to conversion with love.
For regions where Christ is not known.
For the sick, that Christ may heal them as in Galilee.
For those confused by false teachings.
For our group, that we may grow in true conversion.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son brought light to Galilee of the Gentiles. Let his light shine in us and through us, and keep us faithful to his Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God is love, and he loved us first.
Jesus has compassion on the crowd like a shepherd.
He multiplies our little when we give it to him.
2027-01-05.action: Give a meal or groceries to a family in need this week.
2027-01-05.question: What are my five loaves that Jesus is asking me to give?

family.explain: Many hungry people followed Jesus. A few loaves and fish were all they had. Jesus blessed them, and everyone ate until they were full!
family.intention: We pray for children who go to bed hungry.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share with someone this week?”

illus: In a parish in Palakkad, a widow began cooking one extra packet of rice each day for a sick neighbour. Others heard and joined her. A year later the parish kitchen was feeding forty people daily. It began with one packet given with love.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you had compassion on the crowd and fed them with your word and with bread. Feed us now, and make us generous. Amen.
share: God is love (1 John 4:8). How have I experienced God's love this week?
He had compassion for them (Mark 6:34). Whom do I find it hard to have compassion for?
You give them something to eat (Mark 6:37). What can I give?
interc: For the Church, that she may show the compassion of the Good Shepherd.
For the hungry and the poor of our land.
For farmers and all who produce our food.
For those who feel like sheep without a shepherd.
For our group, that we may share what we have.
pm.close: Lord God, you are love, and you loved us first. Make us share our bread and our lives, as your Son shared himself with us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus is the Anointed One, sent to the poor and the captive.
God's word is fulfilled today.
We cannot love God and hate our brother.
2027-01-07.action: Make peace with a family member you have been cold towards.
2027-01-07.question: Is God's word fulfilled “today” in my life, or only remembered?

family.explain: In his home town Jesus read from the Bible in the synagogue. He said: God's Spirit sent me to help the poor and free those who are in prison. Today it is happening!
family.intention: We pray for prisoners and their families.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we bring good news to someone poor or sad this week?”

illus: A prison chaplain in Kannur reads Luke 4 with inmates every Christmas season. One year a man serving a life sentence said: if Jesus came for captives, then he came for me. He began studying, became a teacher for other prisoners, and now leads their Sunday prayer.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, the Spirit of the Lord is upon you. Speak your word to us today, and let it be fulfilled in our lives. Amen.
share: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me (Luke 4:18). Where do I see the Spirit at work today?
Today this scripture has been fulfilled (Luke 4:21). What word of God do I need to let come true in me?
We love because he first loved us (1 John 4:19). Whom do I find hard to love?
pm.resp: Lord, let your word be fulfilled today.
interc: For the poor, that they may hear good news through the Church.
For prisoners and captives, that they may find freedom in Christ.
For the blind and the sick.
For confessors and canon lawyers, through the prayers of St Raymond.
For our group, that our love for God may be seen in love for one another.
pm.close: Lord God, you anointed your Son with the Holy Spirit to bring good news to the poor. Let his word be fulfilled today in us, and make our love for you visible in love for our neighbour. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The leper trusts Jesus' power and asks for his will.
Jesus touches the untouchable and makes him clean.
Whoever has the Son has life.
2027-01-08.action: Bring to confession the sin you are most ashamed of.
2027-01-08.question: What part of my life am I afraid to let Jesus touch?

family.explain: A man had a terrible skin disease, and nobody would touch him. He asked Jesus for help. Jesus touched him and he was healed!
family.intention: We pray for people with leprosy and other diseases that make others stay away.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone at school or in our street that others leave alone? How can we be kind to them?”

illus: St Damien of Molokai went to live among people with leprosy in Hawaii. He dressed their wounds, built their homes and celebrated Mass for them. One Sunday he began his homily with the words “We lepers”: he had caught the disease. He had touched them as Jesus did, all the way.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you stretched out your hand and touched the leper. Touch us now, heal what is broken in us, and make us your hands for others. Amen.
share: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean” (Luke 5:12). What do I want to ask Jesus to heal?
Jesus touched him (Luke 5:13). Whom do I avoid touching or meeting?
Whoever has the Son has life (1 John 5:12). How do I experience this life?
pm.resp: Lord, touch us and heal us.
interc: For people with leprosy, HIV and other diseases that bring rejection.
For doctors, nurses and all who care for the sick.
For those who feel unclean because of their sins, that they may come to confession.
For the Church, that she may touch the untouchable with Christ's love.
For our group, that we may pray as Jesus prayed in deserted places.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son stretched out his hand to heal the leper. Let his hand rest on us in the sacraments, and make us instruments of his healing. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus is the Bridegroom; John is his friend.
He must increase; I must decrease.
Keep yourselves from idols.
2027-01-09.action: Praise sincerely someone whose success you envy.
2027-01-09.question: Where do I want to increase instead of letting Christ increase?

family.explain: John the Baptist's friends were sad because people were going to Jesus. John said: I am happy! Jesus must become greater, and I must become smaller.
family.intention: We pray that we may be happy when others do well.
family.ask: Ask: “When were you happy because something good happened to someone else?”

illus: At a wedding in Kottayam, the best man spent the whole day running errands, settling guests and making sure the groom was at ease. At the end someone thanked him, and he said: today is not my day; my joy is to see my friend happy. That is John the Baptist's joy.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the Bridegroom, and we rejoice to hear your voice. Increase in us as we gather, and let our pride decrease. Amen.
share: He must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30). Where do I need to become smaller?
The friend of the bridegroom rejoices (John 3:29). Can I rejoice in others' success?
Little children, keep yourselves from idols (1 John 5:21). What idol competes with God in my heart?
interc: For priests and leaders in the Church, that they may point to Christ and not to themselves.
For married couples, that their love may reflect Christ and his Church.
For those caught in jealousy and rivalry.
For brothers and sisters who sin, that they may be restored by our prayer.
For our group, that Christ may increase among us.
pm.close: Lord God, John the Baptist rejoiced to hear the Bridegroom's voice. Free us from jealousy and idols, and let your Son increase in our lives. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a happy and holy new year to you all. The Church begins the year by looking at a mother and her child. On the eighth day of Christmas we celebrate Mary, the Holy Mother of God.

Why such a great title? Because of who her Son is. The child she bore is not a man in whom God lived for a while; he is the eternal Son of God who became man in her womb. One Person, truly God and truly man. That is why the Council of Ephesus in 431 declared that Mary is Theotokos, Mother of God. When we honour Mary, we are really confessing our faith in Jesus.

St Paul says that when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). Time reached its fullness not in an empire or a palace but in a young woman of Nazareth who said yes. And the purpose of it all is that we might receive adoption as children. Because Mary's Son became our brother, we can call God Abba, Father.

In the Gospel the shepherds hurry to Bethlehem and tell everyone what the angels had said. All who heard were amazed. But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19). Amazement passes; pondering stays. Mary teaches us not to rush from one event to the next, but to keep God's deeds in our heart and seek their meaning.

On the eighth day the child receives his name: Jesus, the Lord saves. The first reading gives us the blessing that God told Aaron to place on the people: the Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make his face shine upon you; the Lord give you peace (Numbers 6:24–26). In Jesus, God's face has shone upon us; in Jesus, God's peace has a name.

So let us begin this year with Mary. Let us ponder each day what God is doing. Let us call on the holy name of Jesus. And let us be people of peace, for today is also the World Day of Peace. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us this year. Amen.
kids: Children, today we say Happy New Year to Mother Mary! She is the Mother of Jesus, and Jesus is God, so she is the Mother of God.
Mary kept everything about Jesus in her heart. Tonight, before you sleep, tell Jesus one good thing that happened today.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is our feast. At Christmas Jesus was shown to the shepherds of Israel. Today, at the Epiphany, he is shown to the nations. The Magi from the East represent all of us who were not born into the people of Israel, and who have been invited into God's family.

Isaiah had seen it long before: arise, shine; for your light has come… nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn (Isaiah 60:1, 3). St Paul calls it a mystery hidden for ages: the Gentiles are fellow heirs, members of the same body, sharers in the promise (Ephesians 3:6). In Christ there are no outsiders.

Look at how the Magi find Jesus. First they follow a star; they read God's book of creation honestly. But the star brings them only to Jerusalem. There they need the Scriptures: the prophet Micah says Bethlehem. Reason and faith work together. A sincere mind, open to God's word, finds Christ.

But notice the others. The chief priests and scribes knew the exact verse, yet none of them walked the few hours to Bethlehem. Herod heard the same news and was afraid. Knowledge without worship leaves us where we are; fear of losing our power makes us enemies of Christ. Each of us must ask: am I a seeker, a spectator, or a Herod?

When the Magi see the child with Mary his mother, they kneel and pay him homage, and they open their treasures: gold for a king, frankincense for God, myrrh for one who would die. Adoration is the end of the journey. And then, warned in a dream, they leave for their own country by another road (Matthew 2:12). No one who truly meets Christ goes back the same way.

Today the Church announces the date of Easter: this year 28 March. The star of Bethlehem points to the Cross and the empty tomb. Let us bring Christ our gifts, kneel before him in the Eucharist, and go home this week by another road. Amen.
kids: Children, the wise men followed a star for a long, long way to find Jesus. When they found him, they knelt and gave him gifts.
What gift can you give Jesus? A kind word, a prayer, sharing your toys. Jesus loves your gifts!

homily: Dear friends, after feeding the five thousand, Jesus sends his disciples ahead in the boat and goes up the mountain to pray (Mark 6:45–46). Even after a great success, he goes to the Father in prayer.

In the night the disciples are straining at the oars, for the wind is against them. Mark tells us that Jesus saw them (Mark 6:48). From the mountain, in the dark, he sees them. He sees you too, when life is hard work against the wind.

Early in the morning he comes walking on the sea. They think it is a ghost and cry out. Then he says: take heart, it is I; do not be afraid (Mark 6:50). The words it is I are the name of God revealed to Moses. The Lord of the sea climbs into their little boat, and the wind ceases.

Yet Mark says their hearts were hardened; they did not understand about the loaves. We too can see many signs of God's love and still be afraid. St John gives the remedy: there is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18).

Today, in many places, the Church celebrates the Epiphany, and our Eastern brothers and sisters celebrate the Baptism of the Lord. Christ is revealed as the one who comes to us in every storm. Let us invite him into our boat, and let his love drive out our fear. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus walked on the water to help his friends in the storm. When you are scared, say: Jesus, I trust in you! He is always near.

homily: Dear friends, on the second day of the new year the Gospel asks a simple question: who are you? The priests and Levites come to John the Baptist and ask him this. John first says what he is not: I am not the Messiah, not Elijah, not the prophet (John 1:20–21).

Then he says who he is: I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord (John 1:23). A voice exists to carry a word. John knows that his whole life is to carry Christ to others. That is true humility: not hating ourselves, but knowing that we live for someone greater.

St John in the first reading tells us to let what we heard from the beginning abide in us (1 John 2:24). Many voices around us offer a new gospel. The Church asks us to stay with the faith of the Apostles.

Today we remember Saints Basil and Gregory, two friends from Cappadocia in present-day Turkey. They studied together in Athens, prayed together as monks, and became bishops. They defended the truth that Jesus is truly God and that the Holy Spirit is truly God. Gregory said that in Athens they knew only two roads: the road to church and the road to school.
Let us ask for John's humility and for holy friendships like theirs. Let our words and our lives say: not me, but Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist said: I am only a voice; Jesus is the important one! Today let us help someone to know Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, after the Epiphany the Church follows the light as it spreads. Jesus leaves Nazareth and makes his home in Capernaum, by the Sea of Galilee. Matthew calls this region Galilee of the Gentiles, a border land where Jews and pagans lived side by side.

There Isaiah's words come true: the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light (Matthew 4:16). Jesus does not start in Jerusalem, among the important people. He starts on the margins, where people felt far from God.

His first word is: repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near (Matthew 4:17). To repent means to turn around. God has come close; we must turn to face him. Then Jesus heals every disease and sickness, and crowds come from everywhere.

St John warns us to test the spirits (1 John 4:1). Not every voice that speaks of God leads to God. The test is simple: does it confess Jesus Christ come in the flesh? Does it lead to the Church, the sacraments, love of neighbour?
Let us welcome the light today. Let us turn from one thing that keeps us in darkness. And let us take courage: the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world (1 John 4:4). Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is like a big light that came to people who were in the dark. When we say sorry and do good, we let his light shine in us!

homily: Dear friends, St John today writes the most famous sentence of his letter: God is love (1 John 4:8). Not only does God love; love is what God is, from all eternity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

And John tells us where we can see this love: in this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son (1 John 4:10). Our love is always a reply. Before we ever prayed, God loved us.

In the Gospel Jesus sees a great crowd and has compassion for them, because they are like sheep without a shepherd (Mark 6:34). He first teaches them, feeding their minds and hearts. Then evening comes and they are hungry.

The disciples say: send them away. Jesus says: you give them something to eat (Mark 6:37). They have only five loaves and two fish. Jesus takes them, looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks and gives. Five thousand eat and twelve baskets are left over. Our little in his hands becomes enough.
These are the words of the Last Supper and of every Mass: took, blessed, broke, gave. Let us bring our five loaves today, our time, our money, our talents, and let him multiply them for others. Amen.
kids: Children, a boy gave Jesus five loaves and two fish, and Jesus fed thousands of people! When you share, Jesus can do great things with your little gift.

homily: Dear friends, Jesus returns to Galilee filled with the power of the Spirit, and on the sabbath he goes to the synagogue of Nazareth, as was his custom (Luke 4:14–16). He is handed the scroll of the prophet Isaiah.

He reads: the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor, to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free (Luke 4:18). Then he sits down, and every eye is fixed on him.

And he says: today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing (Luke 4:21). Not one day in the future, not only in the past: today. The word of God is alive. When we hear it at Mass, Christ himself is speaking to us.

St John adds: we love because he first loved us. Those who say, I love God, and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars (1 John 4:19–20). The programme of Nazareth, good news to the poor, freedom for captives, must become our programme.

Today we remember St Raymond of Penyafort, who helped ransom Christian captives and spent his life as a confessor, setting sinners free. May the word of God be fulfilled today in us, in love for the poor and in peace with our brothers and sisters. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus read from the Bible and said: today God's promise comes true! When we help the poor and are kind, God's word comes true in us too.

homily: Dear friends, in one of the towns a man covered with leprosy sees Jesus, falls on his face and begs: Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean (Luke 5:12). He does not doubt Jesus' power. He only asks whether Jesus wants to.

Jesus answers first with his hand. He stretches it out and touches him. By the Law, touching a leper made a person unclean. But with Jesus the opposite happens: his holiness flows into the sick man. I do choose. Be made clean (Luke 5:13). Immediately the leprosy leaves him.
Then Jesus sends him to the priest. Healing is not only for the body; the man must be restored to his family and his community. God's mercy always brings us back to belonging.

Luke adds that crowds came to hear and be healed, but Jesus would withdraw to deserted places and pray (Luke 5:16). St John tells us that God has given us eternal life in his Son; whoever has the Son has life (1 John 5:11–12). In Baptism and the Eucharist, the water and the blood, Jesus still touches us.
What is the leprosy you are ashamed to bring to Jesus? Bring it to him in confession. He still says: I do choose. Be made clean. Amen.
kids: Children, nobody wanted to touch the sick man, but Jesus did! Let us be kind to children whom others leave alone.

homily: Dear friends, the disciples of John the Baptist come to him upset: the one you baptised is baptising, and all are going to him (John 3:26). They feel their master is losing out.

John answers with great freedom. No one can receive anything except what has been given from heaven. Then he uses a wedding image: the bride belongs to the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom stands and hears him and rejoices greatly at his voice (John 3:29). John is the best man, not the groom.

And he says the sentence that sums up his life: he must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30). Jealousy is one of the great sicknesses of parishes, families and workplaces. John shows the cure: joy that Christ is loved, even if I am forgotten.

St John's letter ends with confidence and a warning. If we ask anything according to his will, he hears us (1 John 5:14). And: little children, keep yourselves from idols (1 John 5:21). An idol is anything that takes God's place, including my own importance.
Tomorrow we celebrate the Baptism of the Lord, when John baptises Jesus in the Jordan. Let us prepare by letting Christ grow larger in our lives, and our pride grow smaller. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist was happy when people loved Jesus more than him. Let us be happy when our friends do well!

intro: Theme: “Born of a woman, so that we might be children of God.”
Mary's divine motherhood, our adoption, and God's blessing for the new year.

sub: The child is the eternal Son.
Honouring Mary protects the truth about Jesus.
q: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly today, weighing the words “Mother of God”.

sub: Born under the law to redeem us.
q: As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you; you shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, in order to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children.
points.apply: Begin each prayer this week with the word “Abba, Father”.

q: The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
points.apply: Write one line each night on what God did that day.

concl: Mary gives us Jesus, and Jesus makes us children of the Father.
Let us begin the year with her, blessed and at peace.
2027-01-01.resolve: Bless your family with Numbers 6:24–26 on every first day of the month this year.

intro: Theme: “Nations shall come to your light.”
Christ revealed to the nations; seeking, finding and adoring.

points.h: A light for all the nations
sub: Isaiah's vision of the nations streaming in.
Paul's mystery: the Gentiles are fellow heirs.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
that is, the Gentiles have become fellow heirs, members of the same body, and sharers in the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel.
points.apply: Pray for one person who does not yet know Christ.

sub: The scribes know but do not go.
q: Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
asking, “Where is the child who has been born king of the Jews? For we observed his star at its rising, and have come to pay him homage.”
points.apply: Read one chapter of a Gospel each day this month.

sub: They knelt and paid him homage.
q: May all kings fall down before him, all nations give him service.

When they saw that the star had stopped, they were overwhelmed with joy. On entering the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother; and they knelt down and paid him homage. Then, opening their treasure chests, they offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
points.apply: Spend fifteen minutes in adoration before the Blessed Sacrament this week.

concl: The star leads to the Child; the Child leads to the Cross and the empty tomb.
Whoever adores Christ cannot go back the same way.
2027-01-03.resolve: Bless your home this week and offer Christ one concrete gift.

intro: Theme: “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
Christ comes across the storm; love casts out fear.

sub: He sees them in the dark.
q: He will not let your foot be moved; he who keeps you will not slumber. He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
After saying farewell to them, he went up on the mountain to pray.
points.apply: Pray each night this week for those who are struggling.

q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
for they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke to them and said, “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
points.apply: Repeat “Jesus, I trust in you” when fear rises.

sub: Hearts hardened in spite of signs.
God lives in us when we love.
q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear; for fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not reached perfection in love.
points.apply: Do one act of love toward someone you fear.

concl: The Lord of the sea climbs into our small boat.
Where love lives, fear loses its grip.
2027-01-06.resolve: Pray Psalm 27 each morning this week.

intro: Theme: “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness.”
John points to Christ; Basil and Gregory defend the faith.

sub: John says what he is not.
He says who he is: a voice.
A voice exists for the Word.
q: A voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
He said, “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’” as the prophet Isaiah said.
points.apply: Let one conversation today point to Christ.

sub: Stay with the faith of the Apostles.
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you. If what you heard from the beginning abides in you, then you will abide in the Son and in the Father.
points.apply: Read one paragraph of the Creed in the Catechism this week.

q: For the LORD gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding;
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Thank God for a friend who strengthens your faith.

concl: We are voices; Christ is the Word.
Faithful to what we heard, humble like John.
2027-01-02.resolve: Pray the Creed slowly each morning this week.

intro: Theme: “The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light.”
The light moves out into Galilee; conversion and discernment.

sub: God begins where people feel far away.
q: I am the LORD, I have called you in righteousness, I have taken you by the hand and kept you; I have given you as a covenant to the people, a light to the nations, to open the eyes that are blind, to bring out the prisoners from the dungeon, from the prison those who sit in darkness.
the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light, and for those who sat in the region and shadow of death light has dawned.
points.apply: Visit or call someone who lives on the margins of your parish.

q: Cast away from you all the transgressions that you have committed against me, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! Why will you die, O house of Israel?
From that time Jesus began to proclaim, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
points.apply: Go to confession this month.

sub: Not every voice is from God.
Christ in the flesh is the test.
The one in you is greater.
q: I will tell of the decree of the LORD: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.
Little children, you are from God, and have conquered them; for the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.
points.apply: Check one religious message against Church teaching before sharing it.

concl: The light that the Magi saw now walks through Galilee.
Turn to it, and test every other light by it.
2027-01-04.resolve: Read Matthew 4 slowly this evening and pray for those in darkness.

intro: The compassion of the Shepherd who feeds his flock.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.
As he went ashore, he saw a great crowd; and he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.
points.apply: Notice one person in need today before they ask.

points.h: You give them something to eat
sub: The disciples want to send them away.
q: But his servant said, “How can I set this before a hundred people?” So he repeated, “Give it to the people and let them eat, for thus says the LORD, ‘They shall eat and have some left.’”
But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They said to him, “Are we to go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give it to them to eat?”
points.apply: Give food to a family in need this week.

q: the LORD appeared to him from far away. I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God; everyone who loves is born of God and knows God. Whoever does not love does not know God, for God is love.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for three signs of his love.

concl: The miracle of the loaves continues at every altar.
2027-01-05.resolve: Share a meal with someone in need this week.

intro: Theme: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
The Anointed One at Nazareth; love of God shown in love of neighbour.

sub: Jesus returns in the power of the Spirit.
He is the Christ, the Anointed.
q: The spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free,
points.apply: Pray for those who are poor, captive or blind in our town.

sub: Christ speaks when the Scriptures are read.
q: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. O that today you would listen to his voice!
Then he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
points.apply: Choose one verse from today's readings and live it today.

sub: We love because he first loved us.
No split between God and neighbour.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
Those who say, “I love God,” and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars; for those who do not love a brother or sister whom they have seen, cannot love God whom they have not seen.
points.apply: Make peace with one person this week.

concl: The programme of Nazareth becomes our programme.
Today, not tomorrow, God's word wants to come true in us.
2027-01-07.resolve: Do one work of mercy for a poor or imprisoned person this month.

intro: Theme: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”
The touch of Jesus heals and restores; whoever has the Son has life.

sub: The leper believes in Jesus' power.
He asks only about his will.
q: So he went down and immersed himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God; his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.
Once, when he was in one of the cities, there was a man covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he bowed with his face to the ground and begged him, “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”
points.apply: Pray today: Lord, if you choose, heal me.

sub: He restores the man to the community.
q: Surely he has borne our infirmities and carried our diseases; yet we accounted him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
Then Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, “I do choose. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
points.apply: Visit a sick person whom few people visit.

q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.
points.apply: Go to confession and receive the Eucharist with new faith.

concl: Jesus still says: I do choose.
His touch reaches us in the sacraments.
2027-01-08.resolve: Make a good confession before the Baptism of the Lord on Sunday.

intro: Theme: “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
The joy of the Bridegroom's friend; prayer and freedom from idols.

sub: John is the friend who rejoices.
q: For as a young man marries a young woman, so shall your builder marry you, and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you.
He who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. For this reason my joy has been fulfilled.
points.apply: Married couples: renew your vows in prayer together this week.

q: Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory, for the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Praise someone whose success you envy.

sub: He hears us when we ask by his will.
Pray for a brother who sins.
q: you shall have no other gods before me.

And this is the boldness we have in him, that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us. And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have obtained the requests made of him.
points.apply: Name one idol in your life and give it back to God.

concl: John's joy is complete when Christ is loved.
Let Christ grow, and every idol shrink.
2027-01-09.resolve: Prepare for the Baptism of the Lord by renewing your baptismal promises tonight.
